questions.question: Sub-topic: Angular Momentum Quantization. An electron in a hydrogen atom is in a state with orbital quantum number $l = 2$. What are the magnitude $L$ of its orbital angular momentum and the maximum possible value of its z-component, $(L_z)_{\text{max}}$?

Sub-topic: Blackbody Radiation. An ideal blackbody radiator has its absolute temperature doubled from $T$ to $2T$. What happens to the peak emission wavelength $\lambda_{\text{max}}$ and the total emitted power per unit area $P/A$?
options: $\lambda_{\text{max}}$ doubles, while total power per unit area increases by a factor of 4.
$\lambda_{\text{max}}$ is halved, while total power per unit area increases by a factor of 16.
$\lambda_{\text{max}}$ is halved, while total power per unit area increases by a factor of 8.
$\lambda_{\text{max}}$ doubles, while total power per unit area increases by a factor of 16.

questions.question: Sub-topic: Compton Scattering. A photon with an initial energy equal to the electron rest energy ($m_e c^2 \approx 511\text{ keV}$) scatters off a stationary free electron. If the photon is scattered at an angle of $90^\circ$, what is the kinetic energy acquired by the recoil electron?

Sub-topic: Damped Harmonic Oscillator. A mass $m$ attached to a spring of stiffness $k$ moves in a fluid offering a viscous drag force proportional to velocity, $F_{\text{drag}} = -b v$. For an underdamped system, what is the exact expression for the angular frequency $\omega$ of the damped oscillations?

Sub-topic: Euler-Lagrange Equations. A particle of mass $m$ moves in a plane under a potential $V(r, \theta) = \frac{k}{r} + f(\theta)$ expressed in polar coordinates. Which expression represents the canonical momentum $p_\theta$, and under what condition is $p_\theta$ a conserved quantity (constant of motion)?
options: $p_\theta = m r^2 \dot{\theta}$, and it is conserved if and only if $f(\theta)$ is independent of $\theta$.
$p_\theta = m r \dot{\theta}$, and it is conserved for any arbitrary function $f(\theta)$.
$p_\theta = m r^2 \dot{\theta}^2$, and it is always conserved regardless of the potential.
$p_\theta = m r \dot{\theta}^2$, and it is conserved if and only if $k = 0$.
